text: Get Aimparency used by outside developers and collect their feedback
description: The repo is public (ISC) but has 0 stars, 0 user interviews and no outside users; Build Week showed a legible user benefit matters. Lower the entry cost (zero-setup init in any repo, importing existing GitHub issues), reach a first cohort of about five external repositories, and capture their feedback in the graph. Also supplies the user evidence the Prototype Fund application lacks (user-research kit exists, tracker empty).

supportingConnections.hypothesis: Seeing a real graph from a URL in seconds is the cheapest first contact for a new user.
An existing project's issues as a ready graph removes the empty-start barrier for outside developers.
Personal conversations with about five maintainers are how the first outside users and their feedback arrive (Felix, per the relationship principle).
supportingConnections.reflection: Not pursued: grant targeting dropped 2026-11-09. Outside users still come through personal conversations (8f002aaf), independent of any application.

supportingConnections.hypothesis: A whole community using the graph daily yields more outside feedback than inviting single maintainers one by one.

Developers who already keep agent specs in tasks.md try Aimparency when one command turns their existing specs into a graph, instead of starting from an empty one. Refuted if, once the import ships and is mentioned in the README, no outside user imports a spec within two months.
A registry listing in the spec/planning category brings the first outside installs without outreach. Refuted if the listing yields no GitHub stars, issues or clones from strangers within six weeks.
Setting it up side by side with one person shows what blocks outside developers, which no internal test reveals.

status.comment:
Felix 2026-10-16: he will try it at Commons Hub.

Outcome: Added a zero-setup entry: `pnpm dev <repo path or git url>` prints an open link (ddc44bbc, review). With that, lowering the entry cost is covered as far as code can go without real users: open by path, open read-only by Git URL, ?repo= links, issue import, protocol spec. Effectiveness: Each piece is verified locally, but none has been tried by an outside developer, so its real effect on adoption is unknown. Lesson: The bottleneck has moved from product to contact. The next step is to invite about five maintainers in the way the relationship principle describes (why this person, what it offers them, their choice). That needs Felix's voice and permission, so further entry-cost features should wait for first user feedback rather than be guessed.
